//: Vesper · RIM LIGHT ON COBALT. A painted dusk: a girl in a black uniform
//1: floating above a cloud sea, seen from behind, lit from behind by a sun below
//2: the horizon so every edge of her burns red-orange; a cobalt sky above, peach
//3: and rose at the horizon, blue-grey fog below. No upstream palette — every
//4: role is sampled from the picture, and `tokens` names each after what it is
//5: there so the mapping stays traceable. THE source for every shell surface
//6: (quickshell/: bar, launcher, OSD, power menu); theme.lua still owns WINDOW
//7: chrome and CI cross-checks it against this.
//8: Two-tone rule, dusk edition two: RIM RED is the frame — island rims, window
//9: border, lock ring, btop boxes — PEACH (the horizon) is every readout, and
//10: the lit skin of the rim (the glow on her legs) is the launcher. This is the
//11: second dusk after harbor, and what separates them: harbor is amber on teal,
//12: vesper is red and peach on COBALT, and the bar sits on a clean cobalt sky
//13: where harbor's sits on teal. Nothing here is amber and nothing is teal.
//14: The rim is softened one step from the picture's #ff2f1f so a 1px edge is
//15: not searing. warn is the rim's yellow highlight saturated; urgent is a
//16: crimson shifted toward pink so it never reads as the frame's orange-red;
//17: `ok` is state in the GROUND's hue, as glacier's is lit ice: the sky lit —
//18: there is no green in the picture. readoutBright is the rim's yellow
//19: highlight, so the active workspace is an emissive gold lozenge
//20: (modules/Workspaces.qml). The upper sky and the fog are the quiet family —
//21: `dim` and `dormant` — the sky printed UP for contrast (as painted it reads
//22: 2.7:1 on `surface`), the fog as it is; every surface that carries them is
//23: cobalt. The ground is the night side of the sky, darker than the deepest
//24: cobalt in the picture; surface, hairline and surfaceAlt are that cobalt
//25: lifted in steps, kept blue, not navy-grey.
name: vesper
//tokens: What in the picture -> role, so a palette bump stays traceable. `urgent` has no token: nothing in the picture is crimson, it is state. `rimGold` is scenery that became state because it already sits where state needs to be: the one yellow thing in a red-and-blue picture is something pending. The rose of the low clouds (#b87c82) has no role; it informs nothing but the horizon's warmth.
//contrast: Measured on the three surfaces that carry type (WCAG, sRGB blend): `surface`; the bar island — fill #081a33 at 0.80 over the cobalt strip the bar covers (#0c4277, a MID blue, brighter than most bar strips; composite ~#092241); the launcher window — `ground` at 0.84 over the picture's centre (#7b8998 → ~#1c2d46). dim 3.7 / 4.1 / 3.6, dormant 4.9 / 5.5 / 4.7, frame 4.3 / 4.8 / 4.2, readout 8.6 / 9.6 / 8.4, readoutBright 11.5 / 12.8 / 11.1, warn 9.1 / 10.1 / 8.8, ok 7.1 / 7.9 / 6.9, urgent 3.8 / 4.2 / 3.7, text 11.7 / 13.0 / 11.4, launcher 5.7 / 6.3 / 5.5. `ground` on `readout` (the lozenge's digit) 10.3:1, `ground` on `frame` 5.1:1; the launcher's selected row (launcher on its own 18% tint) holds 4.1:1.
//effects: Rim light, not neon: no text glow. The panel texture is the rim — `frame` catching the RIGHT edge of every pane and fading in over the last 18% of its width, with a hairline of it on the edge itself — the picture's rim light, from the sun behind her, and it is the signature. 0.35 over the kind's resting 0.30: the island fill is near-opaque over a mid-blue sky, and the band has to read as light on an edge, not a tint.
//bar: Bar identity. Night panels over a dusk sky: islands a shade UNDER `ground` (#081a33) at 0.80 — the strip the bar covers is the cobalt at the very top of the picture (#0c4277), a MID blue, brighter than most bar strips, so the fill has to be fairly opaque where harbor's could be a silhouette — with a 1px rim at 35%, 10px corners (the one radius), no accent line, and a FAINT red bloom (0.16 over 18px): the rim's halo, the one bloom the theme allows. At 20% show-through the composite lands at ~#092241 — `dim` 4.1:1, `dormant` 5.5:1, `urgent` 4.2:1, `readout` 9.6:1, `text` 13.0:1.
//launcher: Launcher identity: a 1px frame in the lit skin of the rim (the glow on her legs and skirt — the rim's shadow side) around night glass (0.84), 10px window, 7px input + rows — the chips' corner. The launcher is the one surface that covers the bar, so it is the one shell surface that wears the rim's skin: its frame and its selected row.
//osd: OSD identity: a full pill — 1px rim frame, a peach track (the readout), 0.8 so the sky still shows under it.
//session: Power-menu identity: 10px tiles with a 1px rim edge at 40%, over a 0.72 night scrim — the dusk stays visible behind the menu, gone to night.
//wallpaper: Shared by hyprlock.conf (brightness) and sddm/Main.qml (1 - brightness scrim). 0.35 with an 8px blur, deeper than the night themes' resting 0.55: this picture is a lit dusk, not a night, and the lock stack sits over the horizon haze, the brightest band of the sky — at 0.55 dormant type there is 2.6:1; at 0.35 every role under the stack clears its target (hyprlock.conf, LAYOUT NOTE). Dusk going to night, which is what the name says.
